screen_requirements.requirement: Show the terms and conditions word for word, with nothing cut, and require an explicit "I agree" before the Aadhaar number is sent

Each of the five declarations of the consent language has its own checkbox. In an Aadhaar flow the second one, creation with a document other than Aadhaar, is left unchecked; checking it leads to creation by driving licence

The healthcare worker's confirmation names the person logged in to your system, filled from that login. The beneficiary's confirmation shows the patient's name dynamically, from what the screen already holds. Nobody types either name
A private entity removes the word "government" from the consent language. A government entity shows it as written
Nothing is sent until the terms are agreed and the declarations and both confirmations are in. Store who agreed, who confirmed and when, against the patient

Offering the consent in a language other than English is optional, and is what CRT_ABHA_103, an optional case, tests. Where you offer it, the screen has a language choice and the text in another language is the facility's approved translation, loaded as supplied and never machine translated
`enrol/byAadhaar` carries the `consent` block with `code` `abha-enrollment` and `version` `1.4`, which records agreement to the terms and conditions
Registration offers "Create ABHA", with Aadhaar OTP as a method

The Aadhaar field takes 12 digits and nothing else. Fewer or more digits, a letter or a special character shows "Aadhaar Number is not valid" on the screen, and no call is sent. Show the number masked once it is entered
The OTP screen names where the OTP went with the masked mobile the `request/otp` response carries in `message`, as the sheet writes it, `*******XXXX`. Never a mobile your system typed in
The OTP field takes six digits and nothing else. The verify button enables itself once six digits are in

An incomplete, wrong or expired OTP shows the message ABDM returned, as it came. On every M1 screen, a message ABDM returns is never replaced by your own wording. The fixed texts the cases quote, such as "Aadhaar Number is not valid" or the not found message of VRFY_ABHA_303, are your product's own and are shown as the cases write them

A wrong OTP keeps the transaction. The person enters the OTP again on the same screen, and the retry carries the same `txnId`. They never re-enter the Aadhaar number, and the right OTP then succeeds. This holds on every OTP screen in M1
Resend stays disabled for 60 seconds after each send, and enables itself after that

At most two resends. A third attempt does not call ABDM and shows "Maximum OTP resend attempts reached. Please try again after 30 mins". Only the Resend control counts toward this limit. A second press of Send OTP is not a resend
The tester note asks that the "OTP Counter should be visible". A Resend control that does nothing visible gives the person no answer at all
A resend reuses the `txnId` of the first send
A communication mobile that is the Aadhaar linked one goes straight on to creation, with no second OTP
A different one is verified by OTP, with the resend and wrong OTP rules above
The communication mobile, whichever it is, is the one the ABHA card and profile show
`isNew` `false` is not a stop and not an error screen. Carry on from that response exactly as for a new account
Show the profile from `ABHAProfile`, the card with `tokens.token` as `X-token`, and the address step with the same `txnId`
The address step stays open for an existing account. A person can create more than one ABHA address for the same ABHA number, so never refuse a new one because one exists, and never state a limit
Show at least three suggestions from `enrol/suggestion` to pick from

Offer a free field for an address of the person's own, with the rules printed beside it: 8 to 18 characters including `@sbx` or `@abdm`, letters and digits, at most one dot and one underscore, neither first nor last. Each rule shows green when met and red when not
An address already in use shows "ABHA address already exists." with two choices: go on with the existing address, or create a new one
After creation, show the 14 digit ABHA number and the ABHA address together with the profile details
Show the ABHA card as the API returned it, and let the person download it. A non-KYC ABHA address cannot download a card; say so rather than showing a broken one
A system that prints its own programme or scheme card instead prints the ABHA number and the ABHA address on it, both required

Before registering, search your own records by mobile, name, gender and age, and by your own beneficiary id when one is given. A full match links this visit to the existing id. A new id is created only when no match holds

screen_requirements.requirement: A new patient is registered from the shared profile automatically, with no click and no data entry, and gets a token in the `on-share` answer

The `on-share` answer carries the token number your queue issued, in `acknowledgement.profile.tokenNumber`, with `status` `SUCCESS` and no `error` beside it. The case expects the patient to receive a token valid for 60 minutes. The specification gives `expiry` as a number and names no unit, so confirm the unit at onboarding before you set it
Match a returning patient on name, mobile, gender, ABHA number and ABHA address against your records
A certain match registers automatically under the existing beneficiary id, and the visit's care context is created under it
An uncertain match may take one confirmation from the operator, a single choice on the screen. Never any typing
No match: a new beneficiary id is created, as for a new patient
The same person sharing a different ABHA address of theirs updates the ABHA address on the existing beneficiary id. No new id
The same QR code, the same ABHA address and an active queue entry: no new queue entry. Only a new token number may be issued under your queue rules, and the existing queue association stays as it was
The QR code of a different counter or queue: a new queue entry for that queue, with the same patient details and a new token number for it
